name: MyBookaro – Appointment Booking Calendar for Directories and Service Businesses
author: mybookaro

sections.description:
Free appointment booking plugin for business directories and service businesses. Customers book online. You approve, or the listing owner does.

By default, customers log in, pick a service, date and open time, and send a request to book. You answer from a dashboard, and they get an email. Login is a setting you can change, and site-wide Auto-Approve confirms bookings instantly.

Who it is for

  • A business directory on the MyListing theme. Book Now appears on service rows, and bookings go to each listing owner’s private dashboard. First you add a services block and an account type for owners. Tested with MyListing 2.16. Not yet tested with MyListing 3.
  • Another kind of directory. If your listings have their own WordPress admin menu (a custom post type), connect them by hand and choose who owns each. Tested with HivePress 1.8 and Directorist 8.11: Book Now appears on each listing and bookings go to its owner. On both, listing owners use the Contributor role.
  • A service business with no directory. A button on your website takes bookings on one calendar. It suits a coach, consultant, trainer or therapist, or a salon, spa or clinic where one person sees every customer.

What it costs

MyBookaro is a free booking plugin with no limit on bookings, services, listings or listing owners. Dashboards show the newest 1,000 bookings. Nothing is locked, and it needs no outside account, API key or WooCommerce.

What you get for free

For customers:

  • Times that fit. The booking form offers only open times long enough for the service, and checks each one again at the moment of booking.
  • Cancel or reschedule. Logged-in customers manage their appointments from their dashboard, up to a cut-off you set. Guests can cancel or move theirs from the link in their booking emails. Whoever takes the booking is emailed.
  • Emails you can edit. Customers get an email when their request arrives, and when a booking is approved, rejected, cancelled or moved by someone else. Guests, if you allow them, get these emails at the address they enter.

For you and listing owners:

  • Appointment scheduling. Set weekly hours with several time blocks a day, so a lunch break stays closed. Choose how many customers can book each start time.
  • Days off. Close single dates or date ranges.
  • Booking calendar. See bookings by month or week. Each listing owner sees only their own, and you see everyone’s in a table in WordPress admin.
  • Reminders you can switch on. Emails go out 24 hours and 1 hour before a booking.

Before new customers can book, choose who can book in Settings > Access, turn on sign-ups or allow guests, and save weekly hours. A one-business site can do all of this in one click with Set up my business. The settings checklist shows what is still missing apart from weekly hours, and the Installation tab has the steps.

What it does not do

  • No online payments or deposits. Prices show for information only, with the currency symbol you set.
  • No Google Calendar in the free plugin.
  • Customers cannot choose a staff member. A salon or clinic with two people working at once needs a different plugin.
  • No screen for phone or walk-in bookings, or for blocking part of a day.
  • No custom form fields. The form asks for name, email and phone.
  • On MyListing, every service takes the same time.
  • Guests have no dashboard. They manage a booking from the link in their booking emails, which can cancel it or move a booking by the hour (not whole-day bookings).

MyBookaro Pro, a paid plugin that needs this one, adds online payments through WooCommerce, SMS through Twilio, reports and CSV exports.

Your data and privacy

Your online booking system stays on your own site, in your own database. This WordPress booking plugin contacts no outside service beyond WordPress’s update checks.

MyListing belongs to 27collective. WooCommerce and its associated designs are trademarks of Automattic Inc. MyBookaro uses all product names on this page only to identify them, with no affiliation or endorsement.
sections.installation:
1. Plugins > Add Plugin: search for MyBookaro, then Install and Activate.
  2. MyBookaro > Setup Wizard: choose your kind of site. The wizard calls this choice a “lane”.
  3. Follow the part below for your kind of site, then the steps for every site.

A MyListing directory

You need a listing type, an Add Listing page, Enable user registration switched on in Theme Tools > User Roles, and either a package or Enable Paid Listings switched off in Listings > Settings. These steps were tested on MyListing 2.16 and not yet on MyListing 3. The wizard detects MyListing. Buttons appear on service rows, so skip the Booking Button.

  1. In each listing type, add the General Repeater preset field. Then, under Single Page > Content & Tabs, add a General Repeater block, set its Use Field to General Repeater, and put mybookaro_services in Custom Block Classes.
  2. In Theme Tools > User Roles, turn on the alternate account type, give it a Role name such as Business owner, and let it add listings.
  3. In MyBookaro > Settings > Access, set Service Provider Role to that type and Customer Role to Customer. Never use one role for both: customers would get a listing owner’s dashboard and could not book on other owners’ listings. To undo it, change Service Provider Role. If access remains, press Remove this access on the same screen.
  4. Listing owners sign up as that type, save their weekly hours under My Account > Bookings > Settings, and add service rows to their listing. A row has no length, so each booking lasts one start interval.
  5. Owners you already have stay on the Customer role, so set each one to MyBookaro Provider on their Edit User screen. That role gets the same dashboard as the type in step 3, and their listings stay theirs, but they can no longer book on other owners’ listings. This was tested with new owners and not with a directory that already has some, so try one owner first.

Another kind of directory

Your listings must be a custom post type other than job_listing, which MyBookaro keeps for MyListing. There is no ready-made integration, so test one booking on your own site.

  1. In the wizard, choose Generic Directory and a preset for who owns each listing (the post author, or a field holding a user ID) and where services come from. Then pick your listing post type.
  2. On the wizard’s Pages step, keep Create new for the booking page and both dashboards. A page you already have gets no blocks added.
  3. In MyBookaro > Settings > Access, set Service Provider Role to the role your listing owners hold and Customer Role to a different role that your customers hold. On HivePress and Directorist, set Service Provider Role to Contributor and Customer Role to Subscriber. HivePress makes each vendor a Contributor. On Directorist, change each listing owner from Subscriber to Contributor on their Edit User screen. HivePress needs pretty permalinks (any setting except Plain in Settings > Permalinks), and System Status warns when they are off. HivePress’s setting that keeps vendors out of the WordPress back end works with MyBookaro: the provider dashboard links to HivePress’s own pages for adding and editing listings.
  4. Each listing owner saves their weekly hours and adds services on the MyBookaro Provider Dashboard page. With the Shared Catalog Directory preset, you add services under MyBookaro > Services instead.

Book Now shows after the listing content if your theme prints that content the standard WordPress way, through the_content. On Directorist it shows below the listing title. If it does not show, or you want it elsewhere, set Booking placement to Shortcode / block only in the wizard’s Services step and place the Booking Button block (bookaro/booking-button) yourself. Do the same on Directorist if a listing uses a custom single listing page. If its header has no title, Book Now shows above the first section instead.

A service business with no directory

The quickest way: the “choose your setup” notice on MyBookaro screens and the wizard’s first step have a Set up my business button. Pick whether customers book without an account or with one, and press it. You become the provider, and MyBookaro makes the pages Book an Appointment, Services, My Bookings and Provider Dashboard, one 60-minute service called Appointment, and opening hours Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00. Then edit the service and hours. It never turns on WordPress sign-ups: if customers book with an account, turn on Anyone can register in Settings > General yourself.

To set it up step by step instead, choose Single Business in the wizard and set Default Provider to the person customers will see. On its Pages step, keep Create new for the booking page and both dashboards. If a notice asks you to run System Status validation, open System Status once you have a service.

  1. Getting Started > Create first service, such as a consultation. Price and duration are under Meta Boxes at the bottom.
  2. Log in as your Default Provider, open the MyBookaro Provider Dashboard page on your site, go to its Settings tab and press Save Settings. No times show until that person does. If they are not an admin, first set them to MyBookaro Provider on their Edit User screen.
  3. MyBookaro > Settings > Access: set Customer Role to Subscriber.

The wizard sets Booking placement to Shortcode / block only, so customers book on the booking page and wherever you add the Booking Button block. To add Book Now to every post and page instead, choose Normal page in the wizard’s Services step. The wizard’s pages also join your menu if your theme builds it from your pages.

Then, on every site

  1. MyBookaro > Settings > Email: check that New Booking Email is ticked, or nobody is emailed about new requests. New installs start with it on. It goes only to the listing owner or Default Provider, with no copy to a site admin.
  2. The ready-made schedule buttons on the hours screen reset the start interval to 30 minutes, so set the interval after them.
  3. To see everyone’s bookings in WordPress admin, open MyBookaro > Bookings. Cancelling in WordPress admin emails nobody, so use the booking dashboard on your site.
  4. Log out and test with a non-admin account that has your Customer Role, because an admin’s test hides role problems. To let strangers sign up, turn on Anyone can register in WordPress Settings > General. On MyListing, use Enable user registration in Theme Tools > User Roles instead.
sections.faq:
Is it free, and is there a limit?

Yes. MyBookaro is a free booking plugin with no limit on bookings, services, listings or, on a directory, providers. Dashboards show the newest 1,000 bookings, and WordPress admin keeps the rest.

Do I need a directory or a directory theme?

No. Choose Single Business in the wizard. It suits coaches, consultants, trainers, therapists, salons, spas and clinics where one person sees every customer.

Do customers need an account to book?

By default, yes. For sign-ups, turn on Anyone can register in WordPress Settings > General and set Customer Role in MyBookaro > Settings > Access, usually to Subscriber. To allow guests, untick Booking Access in Settings > Setup. Guests get the same emails, with a link to cancel or reschedule.

Is a booking confirmed straight away?

Not by default. Each booking arrives as a request to approve or reject, and the customer gets no email until you answer. Auto-Approve Bookings in Settings > Setup confirms them instantly across the site, and listing owners can no longer approve by hand.

Can customers cancel or reschedule?

Yes. Logged-in customers cancel or reschedule from their dashboard. Guests can cancel or reschedule from the link in their booking emails. A moved booking keeps its approval. Set a cut-off in Settings > Setup. There is none until you do.

Can customers pay online, or pay a deposit?

Not in the free plugin, which only shows prices. MyBookaro Pro takes payment through WooCommerce and a gateway, at full price. Neither plugin takes deposits or part payments.

Does it work with Google Calendar?

No. Google Calendar is not in the free plugin.

Does each listing owner get their own calendar and dashboard?

Yes, once you give them access. On standard MyListing that takes a second account type or a role change per owner. One owner’s listings share one schedule.

Does it work with my directory theme?

MyListing has its own integration, tested with version 2.16 and not yet with version 3. Other directories that use a custom post type can be connected by hand. HivePress 1.8 and Directorist 8.11 have been tested this way. Listeo, Listdom and ListingPro have not been tested, and MyBookaro does not connect to the booking features they sell.

Does it work on block themes, phones and Multisite?

Gutenberg blocks and shortcodes were tested on Twenty Twenty-One, Twenty Twenty-Four and Twenty Twenty-Five, and the Booking Button and Booking Form show a placeholder in the editor. Page builder layouts are untested. The form and customer dashboard adapt to phones, checked at 375 px in Chromium. On Multisite, activate per site. Network activation is not supported, and Delete Data on Uninstall clears only the main site.

Do I need WooCommerce?

No. Online payments need MyBookaro Pro, WooCommerce and a payment gateway. The MyListing theme needs WooCommerce for itself.

How do reminders work, and will they arrive on time?

They are off until you tick Reminder Emails in Settings > Email. Customers, including guests, then get them 24 hours and 1 hour before any booking approved after that. WP-Cron needs site visits to send them, so on a quiet site they can be late.

Where is booking data stored, and can I delete it?

In your own WordPress database. Uninstalling keeps it unless you first turn on Delete Data on Uninstall in Settings > Setup, which removes booking tables, posts and roles. Pages, the log folder and some options stay. WordPress’s Export and Erase tools cover customers, and guests who booked from version 1.3.0 on.

What happens if a Pro licence lapses?

The free plugin keeps working. Pro features and updates stop until the licence is valid again.

Is it an official MyListing plugin?

No. MyBookaro is not affiliated with or endorsed by 27collective, the theme’s maker.

Where do I get help?

Ask in the support forum on this page, and say which theme you use.
sections.changelog:
1.3.2

  • Fixed: Save Quick Settings on the MyBookaro overview switched off settings it does not show, among them the spam Honeypot Field, the setup notices, Provider Cancellation Window, the log file, admin booking edits and the Request Received Email, and with Pro the cancellation fee policy, SMS, webhooks and exports. It now saves only its own fields. If you used it, check those settings in Settings > Setup and Settings > Email, and Pro’s tabs: some may be off because of this, not because you chose it.
  • Fixed: the “Enable this email template” box in Settings > Email now turns that email off. Before, unticking it changed nothing. Every template starts on, so no email stops after the update.
  • Fixed: the Approved, Rejected, Cancelled and Rescheduled templates were hidden in Settings > Email while New Booking Email was off, although they are always sent.
  • Fixed: guests no longer get a “Manage booking” button to a dashboard they cannot open. While the booking is open the button is their own booking link; once it is cancelled, rejected or completed there is no button.
  • Fixed: the review invite fills {owner}, {date}, {date_to} and {date_range}.
  • Fixed: wp bookaro cron-run sent every queued reminder and review invite at once, days early. It now sends only the ones that are due.
  • Fixed: “Run upgrade” on System Status opened the Lite vs Pro page. The screen now explains that the database update is failing and how to rerun it from Plugins.
  • Changed: the suggested privacy policy text mentions guest names and emails, gives the real log file location, and no longer mentions a chat retention setting that does not exist.

1.3.1

  • New: guests can move their own booking. The link in their booking emails now has “Change the time”: they pick a day, see its open times and choose one. Your reschedule cut-off and booking window apply, and you are emailed. Bookings by whole days still ask the guest to contact you.
  • New: customers, guests included, get a “We received your booking request” email while a request waits for you. It is on by default; turn it off with Request Received Email in Settings > Email. Not sent when Auto-Approve confirms the booking, because the approval email goes instead.
  • New: guest emails say “View, change or cancel booking” when the guest can move the booking.
  • Fixed: on HivePress sites that keep vendors out of the WordPress back end, the provider dashboard’s create and edit listing links opened wp-admin and sent vendors back to their account page. They now open HivePress’s own pages, and Directorist’s when it has an Add Listing page.
  • Changed: translation files updated with the text added in 1.3.0 and 1.3.1, and the Greek translation covers it.

1.3.0

  • New: guest bookings keep the name and email the guest enters. Guests get the same approval, rejection, cancellation, reschedule, reminder and review emails as other customers, and you and listing owners see who booked. The update adds two columns to the bookings table; existing bookings are kept.
  • New: WordPress’s Export and Erase Personal Data tools find guest bookings by email. Erasing removes the guest’s name, email, phone and notes and keeps the booking.
  • New: guests can cancel. Their approval, reschedule and reminder emails have a View or cancel booking link. It opens a page with the booking and a Cancel booking button, which keeps to your cancellation cut-off and emails you. The link works only for that booking.
  • New: a guest who sends the same request twice is stopped, as logged-in customers already were.
  • New: the bookings list in WordPress admin finds guest bookings by name or email.
  • New: Set up my business, on the “choose your setup” notice and the wizard’s first step. On a one-business site, one click makes you the provider and creates a booking page, a services page, both dashboards, one service and weekday hours. You choose whether customers book with an account or as guests. It never turns on WordPress sign-ups.
  • New: on Directorist, listing owners with the MyBookaro Provider role can add listings.
  • New: on Directorist, Book Now shows above the first section when a listing header has no title.
  • New: System Status warns when HivePress runs on plain permalinks, which stop its listing and account pages loading, and says what guest bookings keep.
  • Fixed: changing the listing type in the wizard keeps your booking and dashboard pages, instead of leaving the new type with none.
  • Fixed: moving from Single Business to a directory in the wizard turns the automatic Book Now back on.
  • Fixed: the notice at the top of System Status is current on the first visit after a settings change.
  • Developer: bookaro_create_demo_site() sets up the demo used by the WordPress.org Live Preview.

  • New: Book Now appears below the listing title on Directorist listing pages. Directorist builds these pages without the page content, so the automatic button did not show there before.
  • Changed: System Status no longer calls the automatic button ready from your settings alone. Until Book Now has shown on a listing, it asks you to open one and check.
  • Fixed: the first System Status visit after a settings change shows the current result, without a reload.
  • Fixed: before you choose a setup, MyBookaro screens show only the “choose your setup” notice, without “Launch is blocked” errors.
  • Fixed: a missing MyBookaro user role no longer makes WordPress log that translations loaded too early.

  • Changed: new installs email the listing owner or Default Provider about new booking requests. Existing sites keep their settings.
  • Changed: on the wizard’s Pages step, empty slots start on Create new, so pressing Next makes the booking page and both dashboards.
  • Changed: choosing Single Business in the wizard sets Booking placement to Shortcode / block only. The placement options now say what they do.
  • Changed: the “choose your setup” notice shows only on MyBookaro screens and can be dismissed.
  • Changed: support links on free sites go to the WordPress.org forum. The Plugins screen links to the docs, the forum and reviews.
  • Changed: the review prompt counts only bookings by customers, not admins, shows after 2 of them, and has a Maybe later button.
  • Fixed: System Status and the settings checklist now find the pages and blocks the wizard makes on Single Business sites.
  • Fixed: the settings checklist ticks the email row only when New Booking Email is on, and the booking row only when customers can book.
  • Fixed: the wizard’s lane step no longer tells every site without MyListing to pick Generic Directory.
  • Fixed: the block editor labels can be translated, and the booking blocks show up when you search for words like appointment or schedule.

  • Privacy: a listing owner’s email and phone are no longer in the page source for any visitor. The customer who books gets them once the booking is made.

  • Fixed: Greek and English translations, a missing plural form, and a translation file header older WordPress versions rejected.
  • Changed: a rewritten plugin page and new screenshots.

  • Guests have no dashboard. They manage a booking from the link in their booking emails, which can cancel it or move a booking by the hour (not whole-day bookings).

MyBookaro Pro, a paid plugin that needs this one, adds online payments through WooCommerce, SMS through Twilio, reports and CSV exports.

Your data and privacy

Your online booking system stays on your own site, in your own database. This WordPress booking plugin contacts no outside service beyond WordPress’s update checks.
